Wizard.protectedInterfaceOriginal: The first cast of each different prepared Spell Matrix in an encounter generates 0 base Dissonance; repeating a matrix builds Refrain normally.
engine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Intelligence is the Wizard class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Wizard levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Intelligence modifier). Wizard spell attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier. Wizard spell save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier.

The Wizard remains three distinct stages: Base Wizard at levels 1-2, Arch Arcanist at levels 3-9, and one Hero path at levels 10-20: Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer. Hero paths are not additional starting classes and their features cannot be selected before their Wizard class-level gates.

SPELLBOOK. At Wizard 1 your spellbook contains six chosen rank-1 Wizard spells. Arcane School Specialization also adds one legal rank-1 bonus spell of your chosen school without replacing one of those six. For this provisional progression, add 2 legal Wizard spells to the book at each Wizard level 2-4, 3 at each level 5-8, 4 at each level 9-12, 5 at each level 13-16 and 6 at each level 17-20. Level-up additions cost no money or scribing time.

LEGAL RANKS. Maximum Wizard spell rank by Wizard class level is: rank 1 at levels 1-2, rank 2 at 3-4, rank 3 at 5-6, rank 4 at 7-8, rank 5 at 9-10, rank 6 at 11-12, rank 7 at 13-14, rank 8 at 15-16 and rank 9 at 17-20. Grand Tier at level 20 is a special casting permission, not a tenth ordinary rank. A Wizard may learn Wizard-list spells from any school up to the legal rank unless a spell itself has an additional prerequisite.

PREPARED SPELL MATRIX. After a long rest, prepare a number of matrices equal to Wizard level + Intelligence modifier, minimum 1, selecting only spells currently recorded in your spellbook and within your legal rank. You cast ordinary Wizard spells only from prepared matrices unless a feature explicitly overrides that restriction. Preparing the full daily matrix set normally requires 1 hour of spellbook study. Matrix Efficiency reduces this to 45 minutes.

DUPLICATE PREPARATION. You may prepare the same spell more than once, primarily to carry different Matrix Mastery configurations. Duplicate copies never create additional first-cast Dissonance exemptions. For Refrain and the protected strain rule, all prepared copies sharing the same underlying spell name belong to one matrix family regardless of modification.

MIDDAY SUBSTITUTION. Once between long rests, you may perform a 10-minute Spellbook Study ritual to replace one prepared matrix with another legal spell from your spellbook. The replacement cannot exceed your legal Wizard rank. Sigil Rewrite and Matrix Mastery may improve this process as explicitly stated.

SPELL ACQUISITION BY SCRIBING. A found Wizard spell may be copied into the spellbook if its rank is legal for you. Baseline scribing requires 2 hours and 50 gp of inks/materials per spell rank, treating rank 0 as 1 for this calculation. Spell Scribing halves both values to 1 hour and 25 gp per rank. Failure to finish the work consumes no spellbook entry but materials already expended during an interrupted hour are lost.

SPELLBOOK LOSS. Losing the spellbook does not erase matrices currently prepared in memory; you may continue casting those prepared matrices until you next rebuild or change preparation. A blank replacement book can be seeded with your currently prepared spells at 1 hour and 25 gp per effective spell rank each. An unprepared spell you previously recorded can be reconstructed from memory with 8 hours, 100 gp per rank and an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 + spell rank. Failure consumes that attempt's time and half its materials; another attempt can be made after a long rest. Recovering the original book automatically restores access to its surviving entries.

ARCANE SCHOOL SPECIALIZATION is automatic at Wizard 1. Choose exactly one of the eight schools. Your spell attacks with that school gain +1 and your Wizard save DC for that school's spells gains +1. You also add one legal rank-1 spell of that school to the spellbook. The source table explicitly supplies seven school passives; the eighth core school, Abjuration, is named elsewhere but its passive row is missing. Its provisional playtest passive is identified below rather than silently presented as recovered text.

ABJURATION, provisional completion for the omitted eighth row: once per round after you cast an Abjuration spell, gain temporary HP equal to PB until the start of your next regular turn. CONJURATION: creatures summoned by your Wizard spells gain +1 maximum HP per Wizard level. DIVINATION: once per long rest reroll one failed saving throw and use the new result. ENCHANTMENT: when a creature fails its initial save against one of your Enchantment spells, a printed control duration of at least 1 round may last one additional round, but every normally allowed repeat save still occurs. EVOCATION: when casting an area Evocation spell, exclude one creature from its initial damaging area; that creature automatically succeeds and takes no damage if success normally halves damage. ILLUSION: gain +2 on concentration saves made to maintain Illusion spells. NECROMANCY: once per turn during a real encounter when a hostile non-summoned creature dies from your Necromancy spell, gain 1 temporary HP; it is not permanent healing. TRANSMUTATION: after casting a Transmutation spell, gain +5 feet Speed until the end of that turn.

PROTECTED DISSONANCE INTERFACE. The first cast of each different prepared matrix family during an encounter generates 0 BASE Dissonance. This exemption affects only base strain. Refrain and explicitly printed strain costs still apply; the suite disables generic Overcast and does not layer historical Burn onto Dissonance. Repeating a matrix family follows normal Refrain immediately. Preparing duplicates or differently modified copies of the same underlying spell never refreshes the exemption.

Core Systems V 2 Resonance Points and spell-rank RP costs are authoritative for Wizard spellcasting. There are no historical spell slots in this pilot. Wizard cards tagged wizard-spell are always-prepared class matrices once acquired, do not consume a daily prepared-matrix position and use the same RP, concentration, Refrain and protected first-distinct-matrix rules as other Wizard spells. Their printed RP cost replaces any generic rank cost; never pay both.

RITUAL CASTING is automatic at Wizard 2. A Wizard spell in your spellbook with the Ritual tag can be cast from the book without being prepared by increasing its casting time by at least 10 minutes. A ritual cast costs 0 RP unless that ritual explicitly lists a consumed RP cost, cannot be used during an encounter and cannot generate or vent Dissonance through ordinary casting strain.

Only one concentration effect can normally be maintained. Starting a second concentration effect ends the first. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; required half-damage rounding is down for this pilot. Spell Tether and the level-17 Tethered Cast are the only Wizard-specific exceptions in this draft, and each has an explicit RP price, duration and one-tether cap.

MATRIX MASTERY MODIFICATIONS. After acquiring Matrix Mastery, each prepared ordinary spell matrix may carry at most one modification chosen during preparation. QUICK SUBSTITUTION: once per short rest, replace one matrix marked Quick Substitution with another spellbook spell of exactly the same rank using a 1-minute ritual instead of the normal 10-minute midday swap; the replacement loses the modification until the next long rest. COMPONENT ENHANCEMENT: when casting a damaging or healing matrix, spend 1 additional RP to add one extra die of the spell's primary damage or healing die to one roll; if the spell has no such die this modification has no effect. MATRIX LINKING: pair two different prepared matrix families during preparation; after legally casting one, the other costs 1 less RP, minimum 1, if cast before the end of your next regular turn, at most once per pair per round. STABILITY REINFORCEMENT: gain +2 on concentration saves caused by damage while maintaining that matrix. A matrix modification never creates another spell cast or proc event.

All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot grant another additional Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Spell copies, Matrix Sharing, Arcane Fusion, Dual Cast and similar effects pay all explicitly required RP and do not produce duplicate resource, cast-proc or action-grant chains beyond their written resolution.

Round recharge counters decrease once at the start of your regular initiative turn even if you cannot act. Extra Actions and extra turns do not tick recharge. Outside initiative, each uninterrupted 6 seconds counts as one tick. Only positive counters can be reset or shortened and each named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

SUMMON COMMAND LIMIT. All Wizard-controlled conjured, raised and bound companions share one damaging/control Companion Command per Wizard regular turn. Spend one Bonus Action to command exactly one such creature to move up to its Speed and use one damaging or control action from its stat block. Uncommanded creatures may reposition defensively and take Dodge but cannot deal damage or impose conditions. No summoned or raised creature can create XP, treasure, RP, Dissonance relief, additional corpses or kill-resource farms.

NECROMANCER STANDARD UNDEAD. Corpse Harvest and Auto-Raise share a maximum of three standard raised minions. Skeleton: AC 14, HP 6 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Bone Shot, range 30 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. Zombie: AC 12, HP 10 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 20; Slam, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. Goblin Thrall, available only from a goblinoid corpse: AC 13, HP 8 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Shiv, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. These are pre-Flesh-Ascendant statistics.

NECROMANCER AUTO-RAISE. Once per round when one of your standard undead minions personally lands the killing blow on an eligible humanoid and your standard-minion count is below three, its corpse rises at the end of the current turn as the same mechanical minion type that scored the kill, if physically possible. A new minion cannot act during that same round. Auto-Raise costs no Action or RP but can never exceed the three-minion cap or generate a new resource, corpse chain, XP or treasure event. Without Infernal Pact only humanoids qualify.

ELITE UNDEAD PETS. Necromancers may bind Boneflayer, Dreadblade and Wraithbound, at most one of each and three elite pets total. They use the same shared Companion Command limit as standard undead. Boneflayer: AC 14, HP 12 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Bone Shards: range 60, Wizard spell attack, 2d6+S necrotic. Fear Pulse replaces its attack: enemies within 10 feet make Wisdom saves; failure Frightened until end of next turn; recharge 3. Grave Miasma replaces its attack: 10-foot-radius point within 30 feet until start of your next turn; enemies entering or starting there take 1d6 necrotic once; recharge 3.

Dreadblade: AC 16, HP 16 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Disrupting Blade: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic; a concentrating target immediately makes its concentration save with disadvantage. On a natural 20 the target is Weakened until the end of its next turn, taking -1 on attack rolls. Dreadblade has advantage on saves against forced movement.

Wraithbound: AC 14, HP 10 + 2 × Wizard level, Fly 40 and hover. While it has not attacked or imposed control since the end of its previous turn it is Invisible; attacking ends that state until the end of its next turn. Wraith Strike: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. On natural 20 the target makes a Constitution save against your Wizard DC; failure Stuns until the end of its next turn.

Flesh Ascendant's bonus applies after the listed base statistics: every undead creature you control gains +2 maximum HP per Wizard level. If at least two of your undead creatures are active, each gains +1 AC and +1 on saving throws. This does not increase the standard-minion or elite-pet caps.

DARK-TRAUMA INTERFACE. Necromancer features involving corpse desecration, infernal bargains, domination, body control or Mind Prison remain subject to the project's existing dark-content and trauma boundaries. A table may fade description to black without changing mechanics. No feature changes a player's real belief, permanently transfers ownership of a player character or silently retires a PC.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Wizard 1 automatically gains Arcane School Specialization, Spell Matrix System and the starting spellbook, then chooses 4 selectable Base cards, at least 2 Active. Wizard 2 automatically gains Counterspell and Ritual Casting, then chooses 2 additional selectable Base cards. Counterspell is not also placed in the Arch selection pool.

At Wizard 3 enter Arcanist, automatically gain Arcane Tradition as an upgrade of the SAME level-1 school rather than choosing another school, and choose 2 selectable Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Wizard 4 grants one eligible Base/Arch choice. Wizard 5 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic School Mastery. Wizard 6 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic Arcane Ward. Wizard 7 grants one eligible Arch choice. Wizard 8 grants one Base/Arch choice. Wizard 9 grants one eligible Arch choice plus automatic Dual Cast.

At Wizard 10 choose Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer and gain 2 Hero cards from that path. ELEMENTALIST EXCEPTION: Elemental Affinity is automatic at path selection and counts as one of those two level-10 Hero acquisitions, so an Elementalist chooses only one additional Hero card at level 10. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. The chosen Final Theorem is automatic at Wizard 20. School Mastery, Counterspell, Arcane Tradition and all progression-table automatic features are never duplicated as selections.

All acquisition gates use Wizard class level rather than total character level. Normal proficiency bonus follows the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. A multiclass dip cannot unlock higher spell ranks, Arcanist cards, Hero cards, Final Theorems or progression-table features.

Class matrices tagged wizard-spell receive a rank in normalized card data equal to maximum ordinary Wizard rank at their minimum class-level gate (cap 9). Printed RP cost replaces generic rank cost. Counterspell is rank 1 at its explicit level 2 automatic grant. This explicit convention closes rank-dependent Counterspell/Dissonance interactions without inventing extra costs.

Cantrip completion: know 3 Wizard cantrips at 1, 4 at 4, 5 at 10, using the shared missing-repertoire fallback. Cantrips are known directly and do not consume prepared matrices. Always-prepared class matrices are additional cards, not extra arbitrary ordinary spells. Class spell ranks and the normalized activation field resolve incomplete source terminology.
workedExample: Wizard 9 example: Intelligence 16 gives M=3, PB=4 and S=2. Assume the authoritative Core V 2 sheet gives this Wizard 32 RP. The Wizard has prepared Fireball, Web, Shield and other matrices; has selected Spell Efficiency; and begins a real encounter with Dissonance 3.

Turn 1: cast prepared Fireball for its normal rank-3 Core V 2 cost of 5 RP, so RP 32→27. This is the first Fireball matrix-family cast of the encounter, so its BASE casting strain produces 0 Dissonance. Any independent Overcast or other risk would still apply, but none is used here.

Turn 2: cast Fireball again. Spell Efficiency reduces the repeat by 1 RP, minimum 1, so this cast costs 4 RP and RP 27→23. Because Fireball has already received its first-distinct exemption, normal Refrain applies to this repeat; the protected interface does not suppress that Refrain.

Enemy turn: an enemy begins a rank-3 spell. Counterspell costs 3 RP, so RP 23→20. The Wizard rolls Intelligence + proficiency against DC 16 under the pilot Counterspell card. Counterspell is a different always-prepared class matrix, so its first cast receives the base-strain exemption; success negates the triggering spell after its costs are paid.

Turn 3: use the automatic level-9 Dual Cast, which is available once per short rest. Cast two DIFFERENT prepared spells of rank 1 or 2 as one Action sequence, paying both costs. If they cost 2 RP and 3 RP, RP 20→15. Each underlying matrix independently checks first-cast/Refrain state, but cast-trigger effects that say 'once per turn' still trigger only once as written.

Turn 4: cast one member of a Matrix-Linked pair for 3 RP, RP 15→12. Before the end of the next regular turn the paired matrix qualifies for its 1-RP reduction. If that paired spell normally costs 3 RP, its linked cast costs 2 RP, RP 12→10. The link changes cost only; it creates no additional spell, Action or Dissonance exemption.
balanceQuestions: Does preparing Wizard level + Intelligence modifier matrices, while also learning the historically broad number of spellbook entries, create meaningful daily planning without making spellbook management too burdensome at high level?

Do Matrix Mastery, Dual Cast, Spell Efficiency, Arcane Fusion and Tethered Cast preserve the Wizard's methodical identity without producing excessive RP efficiency, concentration bypass or cast-proc multiplication?
Are Spellbinder suppression, Elementalist combination effects and Necromancer minion control comparably valuable when tested across several encounters with the same Core V2 RP and rest schedule?

cards.name: Arcane Recovery
cards.duration: Instantaneous during a completed short rest
cards.effect: Arcane Recovery. Tags: base, passive, resonance. Once between long rests when you complete a short rest, restore RP equal to half your Wizard class level rounded up, never above your normal maximum. This is RP recovery, not a second pool, and cannot trigger spell-cast, Refrain or Dissonance effects.

source.originalText: Arcane Recovery: Once per day during a short rest, recover RP equal to half your Wizard level (rounded up), up to your normal maximum.

cards.name: Spell Scribing
cards.effect: Spell Scribing. Tags: base, passive, spellbook. Copying a legal found Wizard spell into your spellbook requires 1 hour and 25 gp of inks and components per spell rank, treating rank 0 as rank 1 for this calculation, instead of the pilot baseline 2 hours and 50 gp. Level-up spells remain free.

source.originalText: Spell Scribing: Copy spells into your spellbook at half the normal cost and time.

cards.name: Arcane Insight
cards.effect: Arcane Insight. Tags: base, passive, knowledge. Gain proficiency in Arcana, or expertise if already proficient. When examining an active magical effect, spell residue, magic item or arcane construction, you may make an Intelligence (Arcana) check to determine its broad school, function or unusual matrix behavior. The Director sets the normal knowledge DC; failure supplies no invented fact.

source.originalText: Arcane Insight: Identify magical effects and items with greater accuracy than non-wizards.

cards.name: Matrix Efficiency
cards.effect: Matrix Efficiency. Tags: base, passive, matrix. Your normal full daily Spell Matrix preparation time is reduced from 1 hour to 45 minutes. This does not reduce the separate 10-minute midday substitution ritual, spell scribing, rituals or spellbook reconstruction unless another feature explicitly says so.

source.originalText: Matrix Efficiency: Reduce the preparation time for spells by 25%.

cards.name: Scholarly Mind
cards.effect: Scholarly Mind. Tags: base, passive, knowledge. You have advantage on Intelligence checks whose primary purpose is recalling, researching or analyzing arcane theory, magical history, planar magical principles or constructed spell formulae. It does not grant advantage on spell attacks, Counterspell checks or general Investigation unrelated to arcane scholarship.

source.originalText: Scholarly Mind: Gain advantage on Intelligence checks related to arcane knowledge.

cards.name: Arcane Bolt
cards.effect: Arcane Bolt. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, universal, damage. Make a Wizard spell attack. On a hit deal S d6 + M force damage. Arcane Bolt is an always-prepared class matrix once acquired and uses the normal first-distinct-matrix and Refrain rules.

source.originalText: Arcane Bolt: Launch a bolt of pure arcane energy that deals force damage to a single target.

cards.name: Minor Conjuration
cards.frequency: At will while RP remains; one object at a time
cards.effect: Minor Conjuration. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, conjuration. Create one nonmagical unattended object that fits inside a 1-foot cube, weighs no more than 10 pounds and is made of common nonvaluable material such as wood, cloth, clay, iron or glass. It cannot be food, poison, currency, a spell component with listed cost, ammunition with special properties or a functional complex mechanism. Creating another dismisses the first.

source.originalText: Minor Conjuration: Create a temporary, small inanimate object that lasts for 1 hour.

cards.name: Arcane Shield
cards.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
cards.effect: Arcane Shield. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, abjuration, protection. Trigger when an attack roll would hit you. Gain +2 AC against the triggering attack and until the start of your next regular turn, potentially causing the attack to miss. Temporary AC from another Arcane Shield does not stack.

source.originalText: Arcane Shield: Create a barrier of magical force that provides temporary protection.

cards.name: Analyze Magic
cards.rangeAndTarget: One magical creature, object or effect within 30 feet
cards.effect: Analyze Magic. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, divination, knowledge. Make an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 + the effect's spell rank, treating a non-spell effect's Director-assigned tier as rank. On success learn its school or magical category, one active mechanical property and whether it is currently sustained, cursed or bound to another effect. Failure reveals only that magic is present.

source.originalText: Analyze Magic: Study a magical effect or item to gain insight into its properties and function.

cards.name: Spellbook Study
cards.effect: Spellbook Study. Tags: base, active, matrix, ritual. Replace one currently prepared matrix with one legal spell recorded in your spellbook. The replacement must be within your Wizard rank limit. This is the normal midday substitution permission; it does not alter the spellbook, create another prepared-matrix position or reset first-cast/Refrain history for an underlying matrix family already cast this encounter.

source.originalText: Spellbook Study: Spend time studying your spellbook to prepare a different selection of spells.

cards.name: Floating Preparation
cards.effect: Floating Preparation. Tags: arch, passive, matrix. Increase your maximum prepared Spell Matrix count by 1. The extra matrix can come from any school and obeys all ordinary spellbook and rank restrictions. It is a prepared matrix for every rule, including protected strain, duplicate-family tracking and Matrix Mastery modifications.

source.originalText: Floating Preparation: Prepare 1 extra spell from any school each day

cards.name: Sigil Rewrite
cards.effect: Sigil Rewrite. Tags: arch, passive-upgrade, matrix. Replace one prepared matrix with a different spell from your spellbook of exactly the same rank without performing the normal 10-minute ritual. The replacement receives no special Dissonance reset for a matrix family already used this encounter and must obey current Wizard rank eligibility.

source.originalText: Sigil Rewrite: Once/day, instantly swap a spell you know for another of the same tier

cards.name: Spell Tether
cards.effect: Spell Tether. Tags: arch, passive-upgrade, concentration, tether. When you begin a second concentration spell that targets only yourself while already concentrating on a self-only spell, spend 3 additional RP. For up to 3 rounds you may maintain both. Whenever damage requires a concentration save, make one save; failure ends BOTH spells. Starting a third concentration effect ends both tethered spells before the new one begins. Spell Tether and Tethered Cast cannot be combined; maximum two sustained concentration effects total. Only one Spell Tether can exist at a time.

source.originalText: Spell Tether: Maintain 2 self-buff spells without concentration (1/rest)

cards.name: Matrix Mastery
cards.effect: Matrix Mastery. Tags: arch, passive, matrix. During preparation you may assign at most one common Matrix Mastery modification to each ordinary prepared spell: Quick Substitution, Component Enhancement, Matrix Linking or Stability Reinforcement, using the exact common definitions in the Wizard engine. Always-prepared class-card matrices cannot receive these modifications unless a card explicitly says otherwise.

source.originalText: Matrix Mastery: Modify spell matrices to change minor aspects of prepared spells.

cards.name: Arcane Tradition
cards.frequency: Automatic at Wizard 3; not a selection
cards.effect: Arcane Tradition. Tags: arch, school, automatic. Your level-1 Arcane School becomes your Arcanist tradition; do not choose a second school. Prepare one additional matrix from that same school each day without counting it against your normal prepared-matrix maximum. It otherwise obeys all ordinary rank, spellbook, Dissonance and duplicate-family rules.

source.originalText: Arcane Tradition: Choose a school of magic to specialize in, gaining bonuses to spells of that school.

cards.name: Spell Efficiency
cards.duration: Until end of your next regular turn
cards.effect: Spell Efficiency. Tags: arch, passive, resonance. After you cast a prepared matrix, the next cast of that SAME matrix family before the end of your next regular turn costs 1 less RP, minimum 1. This cost reduction does not suppress Refrain, cannot reduce Overcast or additional feature costs and cannot combine with itself.

source.originalText: Spell Efficiency: Reduce the Resonance Point cost of frequently cast spells by 10%.

cards.name: Improved Concentration
cards.effect: Improved Concentration. Tags: arch, passive, concentration. You have advantage on Constitution saving throws made because damage threatens your concentration on a Wizard spell. This does not alter the DC, protect a Tether from rules that explicitly end both effects, or prevent Silence, incapacitation and other non-damage concentration failures.

source.originalText: Improved Concentration: Advantage on concentration checks when taking damage.

cards.name: Counterspell
cards.rangeAndTarget: One creature you perceive casting a spell within 60 feet
cards.effect: Counterspell. Tags: arch-source, automatic, wizard-spell, abjuration, disruption. Trigger when a creature begins casting a spell. Make an Intelligence check adding proficiency against DC 10 + twice the spell's rank, treating rank 0 as 0. Success negates the triggering spell after its costs are paid; failure lets it resolve. This is gained automatically at Wizard 2 and is never also selected from the Arch pool.

source.originalText: Counterspell: Disrupt an enemy's spellcasting, potentially negating their spell entirely.

cards.name: Arcane Lock
cards.rangeAndTarget: One door, chest, portal or unattended object within touch
cards.effect: Arcane Lock. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, abjuration. Magically seal the target. Opening it without your permission requires a Strength check or thieves'/arcane-tool check against your Wizard spell DC. Dispel Magic can end the lock. You can designate up to M creatures who can bypass it. This does not make the object physically indestructible.

source.originalText: Arcane Lock: Create a magical barrier that prevents entry or access to an object or area.

cards.name: Dispel Magic
cards.rangeAndTarget: One creature, object or magical effect within 60 feet
cards.effect: Dispel Magic. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, abjuration. Choose one ongoing spell effect you can perceive. If its rank is 3 or lower, end it. If it is rank 4 or higher, make an Intelligence check adding proficiency against DC 10 + spell rank; success ends it. Cleric.protectedInterfaceOriginal: Once per turn, spending 2 or more Conviction on a Rite or Invocation vents 1 Dissonance; prayer changes cadence instead of bypassing Resonance.
engine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Wisdom is the Cleric class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Cleric levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Wisdom modifier) unless a feature explicitly substitutes another ability. Cleric technique attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Wisdom modifier. Cleric technique save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Wisdom modifier.

Conviction is separate from Resonance Points. Base Conviction maximum is 3, automatically becoming 5 at Cleric 9; after a long rest you begin at your current maximum. A completed short rest restores 1 spent Conviction, to the maximum. A completed long rest restores all Conviction. Conviction Pool raises the maximum by 2. Conviction persists between encounters; simply declaring prayer, repeating a Rite, or performing harmless actions outside a real encounter never generates Conviction.

Only explicit features generate Conviction. Sacred Chant, Sermon of Purpose, Doctrine Shield, Dark Conviction and other printed cards are valid generators. A feature cannot generate more Conviction than its text permits, and Conviction can never exceed the current maximum. Summoned creatures, friendly creatures, trivial creatures, repeated corpse manipulation and staged out-of-combat actions cannot be used to farm Conviction.

Cleric techniques use only their printed RP and Conviction costs. All RP is paid from the Cleric's Core Systems V 2 Resonance Point pool. A Cleric technique is not automatically an ordinary spell-rank cast and does not receive Overcast, spell-slot, cost-discount or spell-proc benefits unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Ordinary spells continue to use Core V 2 spellcasting rules.

Protected Dissonance interaction: once on each of your regular turns, when you spend at least 2 Conviction on a Rite or Invocation, reduce Dissonance by 1, minimum 0. The expenditure must actually occur; waived Conviction costs do not vent Dissonance. A single feature expenditure vents at most once even if it spends more than 2 Conviction. No Cleric card automatically adds Dissonance unless explicitly written.

One concentration effect may be maintained at a time. Starting another concentration effect immediately ends the previous one. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; for this pilot, if a division requires rounding, half damage is rounded down. Sustained Cleric effects use their printed maintenance cost and Bonus Action. A control effect that persists for multiple pulses or rounds gives the target a new save at each printed pulse or at the end of each affected turn as stated.

Round recharge counters are set after resolution and decrease once at the start of the Cleric's regular initiative turn, even if the Cleric cannot act. Extra Actions and extra turns do not create extra recharge ticks. Outside initiative, each uninterrupted 6 seconds counts as one recharge tick. Only a positive counter may be reset or shortened, and a named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

Healing cannot exceed maximum HP, does not remove Wounds, and does not restore a dead creature unless a card explicitly says it resurrects. No Cleric feature provides unlimited permanent HP or resource restoration outside encounters. Temporary HP does not stack with itself; use the higher value. Resurrection and corpse-based effects have explicit use limits and cannot generate repeatable corpses, XP, loot or Conviction.

Invocation Attunement is gained automatically at Cleric level 2. Choose exactly one Invocation Path: Radiance, Judgment, Renewal, Flame, Veil or Echoes. Only the selected path bonus becomes active. Divine Invocation uses the mode belonging to that selected path unless another feature explicitly permits a different mode. Changing Invocation Path requires a future explicit retraining rule; this draft provides none.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION FOR PLAYTEST. Cleric 1: gain the Divine Favor engine and choose 4 Base cards, at least 2 Active. Cleric 2: automatically gain Invocation Attunement and the selected Invocation Path bonus, then choose 2 additional Base cards. Cleric 3: enter Bishop and choose 2 Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Levels 4-8 each grant one eligible Base/Arch choice, respecting each card's minimum class level. Level 9 grants one eligible Arch choice plus Bishop's Mandate automatically. Level 10 choose Saint, Priest or Cultist and gain 2 Hero choices from that path. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one additional Hero choice; levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch choice. The chosen Hero Finale is automatic at Cleric 20. ASI/feat milestones remain separate and do not consume these choices.

All acquisition gates use Cleric class level, not total character level. Proficiency bonus still follows normal total-character-level rules. A multiclass character cannot use non-Cleric levels to unlock Bishop, Hero, Invocation or Finale features. Divine commands, visions and social abilities can influence actions only to the extent their exact mechanical text states; no Cleric feature can force a player character to adopt, abandon or profess a belief.

Capacity clarification: the automatic level 9 Conviction increase is a new draft completion so every Hero can pay its 5-Conviction Finale without buying Conviction Pool. Conviction Pool adds 2 at any level, yielding 5 early or 7 from 9. It never fills gained capacity immediately.
workedExample: Cleric 5 example: Wisdom 16 gives M=3, PB=3, S=2. Assume the Core V 2 sheet gives this test Cleric 12 RP. The Cleric knows Conviction Pool, so maximum Conviction is 5, begins the encounter at Conviction 5, Dissonance 3, and selected Judgment at level 2.

Turn 1: Divine Smite costs 1 Conviction, so Conviction 5→4 and RP remains 12. On a hit it deals 2d8+3 radiant damage. Judgment automatically marks the target Judged for 2 rounds, giving it -1 AC. Spending only 1 Conviction does not vent Dissonance.

Turn 2: Divine Invocation costs 2 Conviction and 3 RP, so Conviction 4→2 and RP 12→9. Because an Invocation spent at least 2 Conviction, Dissonance vents once, 3→2. Using Judgment mode, a failed Wisdom save causes the printed 3d8 radiant effect and refreshes Judged.

Turn 3: Healing Rite costs 2 RP, so RP 9→7. It restores 2d8+3 HP to one living ally. It spends no Conviction, so Conviction remains 2 and Dissonance remains 2. If the ally stood in the Cleric's Consecrate zone and Consecrated Ground was known, the target would also regain the printed S=2 bonus HP.
Turn 4: Sacred Chant costs 1 RP to start, so RP 7→6. Its first pulse occurs, but generates no Conviction yet. The Cleric concentrates on the Chant. Conviction stays 2.

Turn 5: The Cleric maintains Sacred Chant with a Bonus Action. Because Sermon of Purpose is known, the second pulse generates 1 Conviction, 2→3. The Cleric then uses Divine Smite as the normal Action, spending 1 Conviction, 3→2. RP remains 6 and Dissonance remains 2 because no single Rite or Invocation expenditure of at least 2 Conviction occurred this turn.
balanceQuestions: Does a 3-point base Conviction cap, or 5 with Conviction Pool, create meaningful expenditure choices without making Sacred Chant mandatory in every encounter?
Do Bishop's Mandate, Miraculous Channel and the six Invocation modes create excessive burst or action compression when combined, especially at levels 7-10?

Across Saint, Priest and Cultist, are healing, control, resurrection and Conviction regeneration sufficiently bounded across multiple encounters without making ordinary Core V2 spellcasting irrelevant?

cards.name: Conviction Pool
cards.effect: Conviction Pool. Tags: conviction, passive. Increase your Conviction maximum by 2. This changes only the maximum; it does not immediately restore spent Conviction when acquired during play. A long rest restores Conviction to the new maximum.

source.originalText: Conviction Pool: +2 max Conviction cap.

cards.name: Consecrated Ground
cards.effect: Consecrated Ground. Tags: rite, healing, passive. Whenever one of your healing Rites restores HP to a living creature standing in terrain created by your Consecrate feature, that creature regains S additional HP. Apply this once per creature per Rite pulse; it is flat healing and is not itself another healing trigger.

source.originalText: Consecrated Ground: Healing allies on terrain you sanctify (via Rite) heals for +10%.

cards.name: Judging Light
cards.effect: Judging Light. Tags: smite, passive. When your Divine Smite damages a creature currently affected by a Cursed or Weakened condition, add S d4 radiant damage to that Smite. Roll these dice once as part of the Smite; they do not create a second hit or trigger.

source.originalText: Judging Light: Smite deals +20% bonus damage to enemies afflicted by Cursed or Weakened effects.

cards.name: Fervent Ritualist
cards.effect: Fervent Ritualist. Tags: rite, ritual, passive. When a Rite with a Ritual activation normally requires at least 10 minutes, reduce its required time by 1 minute for each full 10 minutes of its printed casting time. This never reduces a Ritual below 1 minute and does not alter Action, Bonus Action or Reaction Rites.

source.originalText: Fervent Ritualist: +10% faster channel speed on all Rites.

cards.name: Invocation Attunement
cards.effect: Invocation Attunement. Tags: invocation, core. At Cleric level 2 choose exactly one Invocation Path: Radiance, Judgment, Renewal, Flame, Veil or Echoes. You automatically gain that path's listed bonus. Divine Invocation thereafter uses that path's mode unless another feature explicitly overrides it.

source.originalText: Invocation Attunement: Choose one Invocation Path (see below); gain a permanent passive tied to it.

cards.name: Radiance
cards.frequency: Automatic only if Radiance was selected
cards.effect: Invocation Path — Radiance. Tags: invocation, radiance, healing. Once on each of your turns when one of your Rites restores HP to at least one living creature, choose one creature healed by that Rite. It regains S additional HP and may immediately end either Frightened or Poisoned on itself.

source.originalText: Radiance: +10% healing power and heals cleanse minor conditions.

cards.name: Judgment
cards.frequency: Automatic only if Judgment was selected
cards.effect: Invocation Path — Judgment. Tags: invocation, judgment, smite. When your Divine Smite deals damage to a creature, mark it Judged for 2 rounds. A Judged creature has -1 AC. Further applications refresh the duration but do not increase the AC penalty.

source.originalText: Judgment: Smites mark enemies with Judged for 2 rounds, reducing their AC by 1.

cards.name: Renewal
cards.frequency: Automatic only if Renewal was selected
cards.effect: Invocation Path — Renewal. Tags: invocation, renewal, healing, rite. Once per use of a healing Rite, choose one creature that actually regained HP from it. That creature also restores 5 Stamina, not exceeding its Stamina maximum. A creature without a Stamina resource receives no secondary benefit.

source.originalText: Renewal: Healing Rites restore 5 stamina to the target.

cards.name: Flame
cards.rangeAndTarget: One creature damaged by your Smite or Rite
cards.frequency: At most once on each of your turns
cards.effect: Invocation Path — Flame. Tags: invocation, flame. Immediately after your Smite or Rite damages a creature, you may spend 1 Conviction. The target ignites and takes 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of its next 2 turns. Reapplying Flame refreshes the duration; the burning damage does not stack.

source.originalText: Flame: Conviction can be consumed to ignite targets for 2 turns (fire DoT).

cards.name: Veil
cards.frequency: Automatic only if Veil was selected
cards.effect: Invocation Path — Veil. Tags: invocation, veil, sight. You can see invisible and ethereal creatures and objects within 30 feet that are not behind total cover. This does not reveal mundane disguises, automatically defeat illusions, or let you see through opaque barriers.

source.originalText: Veil: Gain passive True Sight vs invisible or ethereal creatures.

cards.name: Echoes
cards.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
cards.frequency: At most one pending Echoes-path repeat
cards.effect: Invocation Path — Echoes. Tags: invocation, echoes. Once on each of your turns after a Smite or Rite produces rolled immediate damage or healing, store one original target and that raw dice total. At the start of your next regular turn, if the target is legal, repeat floor(raw dice total/10), minimum 1 for a positive total, as the same damage or healing type. This repeat carries no conditions, resources or triggers.

source.originalText: Echoes: 10% of healing or damage is repeated 1 turn later (Echo Effect).

cards.name: Divine Smite
cards.effect: Divine Smite. Tags: smite, divine. Make a Cleric technique attack against one enemy. On a hit, deal S d8 + M radiant damage. This is one damage event. Invocation Path bonuses and features explicitly referring to Smite may modify it.

source.originalText: Divine Smite: Channel divine energy into a powerful strike against a single enemy, dealing damage based on your Wisdom and consuming 1 Conviction.

cards.name: Healing Rite
cards.effect: Healing Rite. Tags: rite, healing. One living ally regains S d8 + M HP. It cannot restore a dead creature or remove Wounds. Consecrated Ground and appropriate Invocation Path bonuses may modify this healing.

source.originalText: Healing Rite: A channeled ability that restores health to an ally, with increased effectiveness on consecrated ground.

cards.name: Sacred Chant
cards.effect: Sacred Chant. Tags: chant, sustained, conviction. Pulse on start and once when maintained on each later regular turn with a Bonus Action. Under the base feature, the third pulse generates 1 Conviction. Only a real encounter can generate Conviction this way. Maintenance itself does not otherwise heal, damage or grant Conviction.

source.originalText: Sacred Chant: A sustained prayer that generates 1 Conviction every 3 turns while maintained.

cards.name: Consecrate
cards.rangeAndTarget: 15-foot-radius fixed zone centered at a point within 30 feet
cards.effect: Consecrate. Tags: rite, zone. Create sanctified terrain. Your Consecrated Ground feature recognizes this zone. Undead creatures in the zone have -1 on attack rolls. A creature leaving the zone loses that penalty immediately. Only one Consecrate zone created by you may exist at a time; creating another ends the first.

source.originalText: Consecrate: Sanctify the ground in a 15-foot radius, creating consecrated terrain that enhances your healing abilities and weakens undead enemies.

cards.name: Divine Insight
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self; subject matter concerning a religious matter, sacred location or divine presence
cards.effect: Divine Insight. Tags: ritual, information. Ask the Director one specific factual question about a religious practice, sacred location, divine presence or recognized supernatural sign available to your tradition. Receive one truthful fact, symbolic clue or 'unknown' if the information is genuinely unavailable. This never forces certainty about future events or another character's private beliefs.

source.originalText: Divine Insight: Commune briefly with your deity to gain insight about a religious matter, sacred location, or divine presence.

cards.name: Aura of Faith
cards.rangeAndTarget: Allies within 15 feet who can perceive you
cards.effect: Aura of Faith. Tags: aura, bishop. Allies in the aura gain +1 on saving throws. Whenever your Rite restores HP to an ally in the aura, that ally also regains 1 additional HP. Multiple Aura of Faith bonuses do not stack.

source.originalText: Aura of Faith: Allies in range gain +5% healing received and +1 to saves.

cards.name: Sermon of Purpose
cards.effect: Sermon of Purpose. Tags: chant, conviction, bishop. Sacred Chant generates its 1 Conviction on its second pulse instead of its third. A normal three-pulse Sacred Chant still generates only 1 Conviction total unless another feature explicitly extends it or grants an additional generation event.

source.originalText: Sermon of Purpose: Chants now generate 1 Conviction every 2 turns.

cards.name: Liturgical Flow
cards.effect: Liturgical Flow. Tags: rite, invocation, recharge. If you start Rites on two consecutive regular turns, your next Divine Invocation started before the end of your following regular turn sets its printed round-recharge counter 1 lower, minimum 0. This counts as Divine Invocation's one allowed reset or shortening for that round.

source.originalText: Liturgical Flow: Chaining 2 Rites reduces cooldown of your next Invocation by 1 turn.

cards.name: Anointed Guardian
cards.rangeAndTarget: First ally within 30 feet to fall to one-quarter maximum HP or less
cards.effect: Anointed Guardian. Tags: protection, bishop. The first qualifying ally in an encounter gains a ward for 2 rounds. The first time during each round that ally takes damage, reduce that damage by PB + M, minimum 0. The ward does not prevent conditions attached to an attack unless the damage reduction itself invalidates them under another rule.

source.originalText: Anointed Guardian: First time an ally drops below 20% HP per combat, grant them a 30% damage reduction shield for 2 rounds.

cards.name: Sanctified Reprisal
cards.duration: Until end of your next regular turn
cards.effect: Sanctified Reprisal. Tags: healing, smite, bishop. After one of your Cleric features restores HP to a living creature, empower your next Divine Smite before the end of your next regular turn. On a hit it deals S d4 additional radiant damage. If the target is Undead, it must also make a Constitution save; failure Stuns it until the end of its next turn.

source.originalText: Sanctified Reprisal: Whenever you heal, next Smite deals 20% more damage and stuns Undead.

cards.name: Miraculous Channel
cards.rangeAndTarget: Your next ally-targeting Rite this turn
cards.effect: Miraculous Channel. Tags: rite, channel, bishop. Your next Rite this turn that normally affects one or more willing allies may affect up to six legal willing allies within the Rite's normal range instead. Roll shared healing or numeric effects once and apply normally. It does not multiply hostile targets, corpse targets or resource generation.

source.originalText: Miraculous Channel: Sacrificing 3 Conviction causes your next Rite to affect the full party.

cards.name: Bishop's Mandate
cards.rangeAndTarget: Your Sacrament and one legal Divine Invocation target set
cards.frequency: Automatic at Cleric 9; once per Sacrament start
cards.effect: Bishop's Mandate. Tags: sacrament, invocation, capstone. When you legally start Sacrament, immediately resolve one free Divine Invocation using your selected Invocation Path. This free Invocation requires no Action, RP or Conviction, sets no Divine Invocation recharge and cannot itself trigger Bishop's Mandate. The Sacrament's own Conviction expenditure may still vent Dissonance normally.

source.originalText: Capstone: Bishop's Mandate: Activating a Sacrament automatically casts a free Invocation without cost or cooldown.

cards.name: Divine Invocation
cards.effect: Divine Invocation. Tags: invocation, bishop. Use only your selected Invocation Path. Radiance: up to 3 allies within 30 feet each regain S d8+M HP; one may end Frightened or Poisoned. Judgment: one enemy within 60 feet makes a Wisdom save, taking (S+1)d8 radiant on failure or half on success; failure also applies Judged for 2 rounds. Renewal: up to 2 allies within 30 feet each regain S d8+M HP and 5 Stamina. Flame: creatures in a 15-foot cone make Dexterity saves, taking (S+1)d8 fire on failure or half on success; failed targets also take 1d6 fire at the start of their next turn. Veil: up to 3 allies within 30 feet can see invisible/ethereal creatures within 30 feet and gain advantage on saves against illusions for 3 rounds. Echoes: choose one eligible Smite or Rite you resolved this turn or previous regular turn and one original target within 30 feet; repeat 50% of its immediate unmodified rolled damage or healing dice, rounded down once, minimum 1 for a positive source, with no copied conditions, resources or triggers.

source.originalText: Divine Invocation: Channel a powerful prayer based on your chosen Invocation Path, with effects ranging from mass healing to divine fire or protective barriers.

cards.name: Sacrament
cards.cost: 3 Conviction + 4 RP to start; 1 RP maintenance
cards.effect: Sacrament. Tags: sacrament, rite, sustained, zone. Pulse on start and on each paid Bonus Action maintenance. At each pulse, up to three allies in the zone gain +1 on saving throws until the start of your next regular turn or effect end, whichever is first. Up to three Undead or Fiends in the zone make Wisdom saves, taking S d6 radiant damage on failure or half on success. Maximum 3 pulses.

source.originalText: Sacrament: Perform a sacred ceremony that consumes Conviction to create a powerful, sustained effect in an area.

cards.name: Banish Unholy
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to three Undead or Fiends within 30 feet
cards.duration: Instantaneous; banishment rider lasts until end of target's next turn
cards.effect: Banish Unholy. Tags: divine, control. Each target makes a Wisdom save. Failure deals (S+1)d8 radiant damage and pushes it up to 15 feet directly away from you; success takes half damage and no push. A target failing by 10 or more is also banished until the end of its next turn, then returns to the nearest legal space.

source.originalText: Banish Unholy: Channel divine energy to damage and potentially banish undead, demons, or other unholy entities.

cards.name: Blessing of Protection
cards.effect: Blessing of Protection. Tags: blessing, protection. Choose one mode on use. Resistance: choose acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, radiant or thunder; the ally gains resistance to that damage type. Resolve: choose Charmed, Frightened or Poisoned; the ally gains advantage on saves against that condition and may immediately repeat one current save against it.

source.originalText: Blessing of Protection:  Bestow a divine blessing on an ally, granting them resistance to a specific damage type or condition.

cards.name: Commune
cards.effect: Commune. Tags: ritual, information, bishop. Ask up to three questions concerning divine doctrine, sacred duties, supernatural threats or a course of action. For each, the Director answers truthfully with yes, no, unclear or a brief symbolic response based on what the contacted divine source could know. Commune cannot compel a deity, reveal another player's private belief, or guarantee a future choice.

source.originalText: Commune:  Enter a deep meditative state to receive guidance directly from your deity, gaining insight on important matters or divine intervention.

cards.name: Aura of Grace
cards.frequency: Healing once/own regular turn; critical reduction once/ally/round
cards.effect: Aura of Grace. At the start of your regular turn during a real encounter, you may pay 1 RP to heal S HP to up to 3 living allies within 15 ft below half maximum HP. You must be conscious. Separately, once per ally per round when an ally in the aura suffers a critical hit, reduce its added critical damage by one damage die, minimum 0 extra dice. No unlimited free healing.

source.originalText: Aura of Grace: Allies in range resist critical hits and gain minor HP regen.

cards.name: Divine Rebirth
cards.rangeAndTarget: One ally revived by your Cleric feature
cards.duration: Instantaneous plus temporary HP for 1 minute
cards.effect: Divine Rebirth. Tags: saint, resurrection. When one of your Cleric features returns an ally from death, you may use Divine Rebirth. That ally returns with half its maximum HP instead of the feature's normal returned HP and gains S + M temporary HP for 1 minute. It removes no Wounds and cannot affect a creature that was not actually dead.

source.originalText: Divine Rebirth: On revive, ally returns with 50% HP and a temporary resistance shield.

cards.name: Merciful Sacrament
cards.effect: Merciful Sacrament. Tags: saint, sacrament. When you start Sacrament and at least one living ally inside its initial zone is at or below one-quarter maximum HP, you may reduce that Sacrament's Conviction cost to 0. Its RP cost and all other requirements remain. Because no Conviction is spent, this waived cost does not vent Dissonance.

source.originalText: Merciful Sacrament: Sacraments cost no Conviction if used on an ally under 25% HP.

cards.name: Unyielding Light
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to six living party members within 30 feet, including you
cards.effect: Unyielding Light. Tags: saint, emergency, healing. When one damage event would leave every conscious living party member within 30 feet at 0 HP, resolve that damage, then before ordinary death-save progression each qualifying living creature at 0 HP regains floor(maximum HP/3), minimum 1. It cannot revive a creature killed outright and removes no Wounds. This one emergency trigger may resolve even if that event incapacitates you, provided you remain alive; it grants no other actions while incapacitated.

source.originalText: Unyielding Light: Once per day, prevents party wipe and restores 30% HP.

cards.name: Celestial Resurgence
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to six allied corpses within 30 feet that died during the previous 3 rounds
cards.effect: Final Miracle — Celestial Resurgence. Tags: saint, finale, resurrection, rite. Each legal target returns to life at 1 HP. The body must be sufficiently present to sustain life. This removes no Wounds, curses or other death consequences. Divine Rebirth may modify one returned ally if available. The Conviction expenditure can vent Dissonance once under the common rule.

source.originalText: Final Miracle: Celestial Resurgence: Revive all allies who died within the last 3 turns.

cards.name: Mass Healing Light
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to six living allies within 30 feet
cards.effect: Mass Healing Light. Tags: saint, healing. Roll S d8 + M once. Each target regains that amount. A target below half maximum HP when chosen regains an additional 1d8 HP. Roll that bonus once and apply it to all qualifying targets. This cannot revive the dead or remove Wounds.

source.originalText: Mass Healing Light: Channel divine energy to heal all allies within 30 feet, with increased effectiveness on those most wounded.

cards.name: Divine Intervention
cards.effect: Divine Intervention. Tags: saint, emergency. Trigger when the ally either fails a saving throw or takes damage that would reduce it to 0 HP. Choose one: the ally rerolls the failed save and must use the new result; or reduce the triggering damage by 2 S d8 + M, minimum 0. This cannot negate an event that has already fully resolved.

source.originalText: Divine Intervention: Call upon your deity to intervene directly, potentially averting disaster or creating a miraculous effect.

cards.name: Sanctify Being
cards.effect: Sanctify Being. Tags: saint, protection. Choose one mode. Elemental Sanctity grants resistance to one of acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, radiant or thunder. Purity grants immunity to exactly one of Charmed, Frightened or Poisoned. Choose when activated; the choice cannot change during that use.

source.originalText: Sanctify Being: Bestow temporary divine protection on an ally, granting them immunity to specific conditions or damage types.

cards.name: Radiant Burst
cards.rangeAndTarget: 15-foot radius centered on you; up to six allies and six Undead/Fiends
cards.effect: Radiant Burst. Tags: saint, healing, radiant. Roll S d8 once. Each chosen living ally regains that roll + M HP. Each chosen Undead or Fiend makes a Wisdom save, taking the same S d8 roll as radiant damage on failure or half on success. Healing and damage are separate applications of the shared roll.

source.originalText: Radiant Burst: Release a powerful wave of divine energy that heals allies and damages unholy creatures.

cards.name: Resurrection
cards.rangeAndTarget: One allied corpse you touch that died within the previous 1 minute
cards.effect: Resurrection. Tags: saint, resurrection, rite. Return the target to life at 1 HP and grant it 2 S + M temporary HP for 1 minute. It gains no removed Wounds and receives no restored expended resources beyond what another rule explicitly provides. A missing vital body prevents the effect. The Conviction expenditure can vent Dissonance once.

source.originalText: Resurrection: Return a fallen ally to life with renewed vigor and temporary divine blessing.

cards.name: Scriptural Echo
cards.rangeAndTarget: One legal original target of your previously used Divine Invocation
cards.effect: Scriptural Echo. Tags: priest, rite, invocation. When you start a Rite, you may repeat 50% of the immediate rolled damage or healing dice from the most recent Divine Invocation you personally resolved since the end of your previous regular turn. Round down once, minimum 1 for a positive source. It copies no conditions, movement, resource effects, control or Invocation Path triggers.

source.originalText: Scriptural Echo: Casting a Rite repeats the Invocation used previously for 50% effect.

cards.name: Words of Equilibrium
cards.effect: Words of Equilibrium. Tags: priest, scaling. For numeric Cleric technique healing and damage that would add your Wisdom modifier, use the higher of your Intelligence or Wisdom modifier instead. M becomes max(1, that higher modifier) for those numeric effects. This does not change Cleric attack rolls or save DCs unless another rule explicitly says so.

source.originalText: Words of Equilibrium: Heal and Damage dealt scale off the higher of INT or WIS.

cards.name: Balanced Scales
cards.rangeAndTarget: Living creatures healed by your Cleric features
cards.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
cards.frequency: At most once per marked ally per round
cards.effect: Balanced Scales. Tags: priest, healing, retaliation. After you restore HP to a living ally, mark it until the start of your next regular turn. The first enemy to damage that ally during the mark takes S + M radiant damage. The retaliation is not an attack, cannot critically hit and cannot recursively trigger another Balanced Scales event.

source.originalText: Balanced Scales: Enemies take divine damage if they attack healed targets.

cards.name: Doctrine Shield
cards.effect: Doctrine Shield. Tags: priest, conviction, cleanse. During a real encounter, when one of your Cleric features successfully removes Charmed, Frightened, Poisoned or another explicitly removable condition from a living creature, gain 1 Conviction. Removing multiple conditions in the same event still grants only 1 Conviction.

source.originalText: Doctrine Shield: Gain 1 Conviction anytime a condition is removed.

cards.name: Word of Binding
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to six enemies within 30 feet
cards.effect: Final Miracle — Word of Binding. Tags: priest, finale, control, rite. Each target makes a Wisdom save. On failure it is Silenced and its Speed becomes 0. At the end of each of its turns it repeats the save, ending both effects on success. While a target remains bound, the first instance of divine or radiant damage it takes each round gains S d6 additional radiant damage. The Conviction expenditure can vent Dissonance once.

source.originalText: Final Miracle: Word of Binding: Enemies in a large AoE are silenced, snared, and take +25% divine damage for 3 turns.

cards.name: Balance Restoration
cards.rangeAndTarget: 15-foot-radius area centered at a point within 30 feet
cards.effect: Balance Restoration. Tags: priest, healing, radiant. Choose up to three living allies and three enemies in the area. Roll S d8 once. Each ally regains the roll + M HP. Each enemy makes a Wisdom save, taking the same S d8 roll as radiant damage on failure or half on success.

source.originalText: Balance Restoration: Channel divine energy that both heals allies and damages enemies in an area, maintaining cosmic balance.

cards.name: Divine Judgment
cards.effect: Divine Judgment. Tags: priest, judgment. The target makes a Wisdom save; success ends the attempt. On failure it is marked. The first time on each of its turns that it deals damage to another creature, it takes radiant damage equal to half that actual damage rounded down, minimum 1, maximum your Cleric level. It repeats the Wisdom save at the end of each turn, ending the mark on success.

source.originalText: Divine Judgment: Mark an enemy for judgment, causing them to take damage proportional to the harm they inflict.

cards.name: Ritual of Cleansing
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to three living allies within 30 feet; secondary enemies within 15 feet of you
cards.effect: Ritual of Cleansing. Tags: priest, rite, cleanse. Each ally may end one of Charmed, Frightened or Poisoned. For each distinct condition actually removed, choose one enemy within 15 feet; each chosen enemy makes a Wisdom save. On failure it becomes Frightened of you until the end of its next turn. One enemy can be chosen only once per use.

source.originalText: Ritual of Cleansing: Perform a ritual that removes multiple negative conditions from allies while potentially imposing them on enemies.

cards.name: Word of Power
cards.effect: Word of Power. Tags: priest, divine. Choose one mode. Mercy: one willing living creature regains S d8+M HP. Rebuke: one Undead or Fiend makes a Constitution save, taking (S+1)d8 radiant on failure or half on success; failure also removes its Reaction until the start of its next turn. Command: one other hostile creature makes a Wisdom save; failure knocks it Prone and removes its Reaction until the start of its next turn. No mode changes beliefs, loyalty or ideology.

source.originalText: Word of Power: Speak a divine word that has different effects based on the target's nature and actions.

cards.name: Cosmic Equilibrium
cards.effect: Cosmic Equilibrium. Tags: priest, zone, healing, radiant. Once per round, when a living ally in the zone receives healing beyond its missing HP, redirect up to S+M of that excess as radiant damage to one enemy in the zone. Separately, once per round when an enemy in the zone takes radiant damage from one of your Cleric features, one ally in the zone regains up to S+M HP, not exceeding half the actual radiant damage dealt. These two conversions cannot trigger each other.

source.originalText: Cosmic Equilibrium: Create a zone where healing and harm are balanced, converting excess damage to healing and vice versa.

cards.name: Sanguine Rite
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self and one ally within 30 feet
cards.frequency: At most once on each of your turns
cards.effect: Sanguine Rite. Tags: cultist, rite, healing. When one of your Rites deals damage to at least one enemy, choose one living ally within 30 feet. That ally regains HP equal to half the actual damage dealt to one chosen damaged enemy, rounded down, maximum S+M HP. This healing cannot trigger Sanguine Rite again.

cards.name: Blasphemous Tongue

cards.name: Dark Conviction

During a real encounter, when a hostile non-summoned creature that meaningfully threatened the party dies after taking damage from one of your Cleric features since the start of your current turn, gain 1 Conviction. cards.name: Zealot's Touch

Druid.protectedInterfaceOriginal: Entering Shapeshift clears the Refrain counter because the Druid changes the body sounding the Weave; beast-form casting remains limited by class features.
engine: Wisdom governs spells, form attacks and class DC/M. Hit Die d8; book armor, weapons, saves and skills remain. Retain your own ability scores, HP, saves, proficiency and personality in all forms; form traits replace only the stated anatomy, movement and attacks. No additional monster stat block or separate beast HP pool. One natural attack per Attack Action unless a form explicitly states otherwise, attack PB+WIS, printed dice+WIS damage. Missing natural attack is 1d6 bludgeoning; default walking Speed 30 ft, normal AC, Medium size. Hawk is Tiny, Bear/Earth Warden/hero forms may be Large when space permits. Equipment melds and cannot be used while melded; magical numeric bonuses persist only if compatible with form anatomy and never duplicate armor.

This class follows its explicit book progression instead of the ordinary 25-choice template. Base 1 grants Druidic, spellcasting, all five Base forms and 2 shifts/long rest. Choose one of seven Circles at 2; its level 2 features are a Base-stage exception. Enter the chosen Circle Arch path at 3, gain its 6 feature, then Circle Hero forms at 10 and its 14 feature. Arch Forms unlock 11 despite the historical word Arch; these are forms, not a second promotion. At 11 attune up to 2 Arch forms during long rest. Base forms remain available at higher levels. All features below are automatic at their gate for the chosen Circle; no generic extra class-card choices are added.

Preparation: two cantrips at 1, three at 4, four at 10, plus explicit Circle bonuses. Prepare class level+WIS modifier ranked Druid spells (minimum 1) each long rest, rank limited by Druid spell-rank access, not merely by enough RP. Use approved operational spell entries and Core V 2 RP table/costs in the shared configuration. Book rank-times-two cost and imported spell-slot terminology are preserved as superseded alternatives for this pilot. Circle always-prepared spells do not count toward preparation and use ordinary RP/Dissonance. Rituals must have ritual tag, be prepared and take printed casting time plus 10 minutes; waive base RP only, never consumed materials or other costs. ASI/feat milestones 4/8/12/16/19 belong to general advancement and must not be granted twice.

Shifting: Bonus Action, one long-rest shift use, 10 minutes, early reversion Bonus Action. Reaching 0 HP or incapacitation ends form; excess damage stays on your own HP. Shift uses follow detailed book table:2 at 1, 3 at 4, 4 at 7, 5 at 10, 6 at 13, 7 at 16, 8 at 19. Supplemental runtime alternative 2/3/4/5/6 at 1/4/8/12/16 remains preserved. At 20 changing form is unlimited but does not refill finite form benefits. Speech unavailable in Base forms, available in Arch/Hero. No spellcasting in form until Beast Spells 18 except an explicit form permission. Maintaining an existing spell concentration is allowed, still only one concentration. Changing form spends a use and ends old form features/summons; it does not reset once/rest abilities.

Transformation reserves prevent unlimited replacement HP: at long rest record Buffer Reserve=2 L+M and Form Surge Reserve=PB. A form giving temporary HP draws that many from Buffer Reserve, up to remaining amount, with normal nonstacking; never real healing. A form special described once/transformation also spends 1 Form Surge and cannot be refreshed by resuming the form. Form Surge refills only long rest. Forms cannot grant free casts, RP or shift uses. Auras affect at most 3 enemies and once per enemy per round; retaliation once/round total; ongoing riders refresh, never stack. Entering a legal Shapeshift clears the Refrain counter and remembered repeated-spell name, as the protected source contract requires. It does not reduce accumulated Dissonance. Natural attacks do not clear Refrain.

Circle of the Land chooses one terrain at 2. Always-prepared spell pairs at 3/5/7/9 are exactly the source table lines 2662–2669, reproduced in source appendix; their source names resolve to existing approved spell entries before use. They do not bypass rank gates. For this pilot Circle spells are permitted exceptions to ordinary list membership, not newly authored variants. Moon Circle Forms CR table is historical external-stat language: use only these bounded forms, not arbitrary CR beasts. Early Moon benefit is +S damage on first form hit each turn. No imported monster multiattack, spellcasting or legendary actions.

Circle summary: Land preserves lore and recovery; Moon improves shifting; Storm controls lightning and wind; Thorns works poison and roots; Winterfang works cold; Rotshaper uses bounded swarms; Ashen Grove works fire and regrowth. Land/Thorns duplicate Blight Elk and Tanglemaw names are kept as separate source identities. Source auto-failed hostile saves in Master of Decay/Ash become once/turn-2 on one save, not unavoidable control. Stronger supplemental flavor riders are represented explicitly below or retained as unadopted alternatives in source provenance.
workedExample: Druid 5 Moon, WIS 16 PB 3 S 2 M 3: RP 12, shifts 3, Buffer Reserve 13, Form Surges 3, HP 30/38. Prepare 8 ranked spells plus three cantrips.

Turn 1 Bonus Action Bear: shifts 3→2, draw 13 of requested 20 buffer, reserve 13→0, temp HP 13. Action claw attack PB+WIS=+6, damage 2d6+3+1 plus Moon first-hit 2. Shifting clears the Refrain counter and remembered repeated-spell name; accumulated Dissonance is unchanged.
Enemy deals 10 damage: temp HP 13→3, real HP 30 remains. No additional beast HP exists.
Turn 2 Moon healing Bonus Action spends 2 RP, RP 12→10, rolls 2d8=7, HP 30→37. It cannot repair the buffer reserve. Action claw as usual.
Turn 3 Bonus Action change Wolf spends another shift, shifts 2→1. Old Bear temporary HP ends. Wolf bite 1d8+3, target STR against DC 14 or Prone. No new buffer, RP or Form Surge generated.
At 10 this character gains Moon Hero forms; Arch forms still wait until 11. At 20 unlimited changes still cannot refill Buffer or Surge reserves.
balanceQuestions: Is the shared HP model with finite buffer durable enough?
Do level2 Circle exceptions remain clear beside the ordinary Arch3 rule?
Do powerful flight and form resistances require encounter adjustments?

cards.name: Druidic
cards.effect: Know Druidic. Other speakers notice and read your hidden Druidic messages. Nonspeakers notice their presence on WIS Perception DC 15 but need translation magic or learning the language to read them.

source.originalText:
Druidic
You know Druidic, the secret language of druids. You can speak the language and use it to leave hidden messages. You and others who know this language automatically spot such a message. Others spot the message's presence with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check but can't decipher it without magic.

cards.name: Spellcasting
cards.effect: Prepare and cast according to the engine. WIS attack/DC; rank gates, components, concentration, Dissonance and RP apply. This entry creates no extra actions or second resource pool.

source.originalText:
Spellcasting
Drawing on the essence of nature itself, you can cast spells to shape that essence to your will. See chapter 10 for the general rules of spellcasting and chapter 11 for the druid spell list.
Cantrips
At 1st level, you know two cantrips of your choice from the druid spell list. You learn additional druid cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Druid table.
Preparing and Casting Spells
The Druid table shows how many Resonance Points you have to cast your druid spells. A spell's base RP cost is twice its Resonance Rank (Rank 0 cantrips cost 0), modified by explicit class features and current Dissonance. You regain expended RP according to the Resonance recovery rules.
You prepare the list of druid spells that are available for you to cast, choosing from the druid spell list. When you do so, choose a number of druid spells equal to your Wisdom modifier + your druid level (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have Resonance Points.
For example, if you are a 3rd-level druid, you have 7 Resonance Points. With a Wisdom of 16, your list of prepared spells can include six spells, and they can be of 1st or 2nd level in any combination. If you prepare the Rank 1 spell cure wounds, its base cost is 2 Resonance Points before explicit specialization or Dissonance modifiers. Casting the spell doesn't remove it from your list of prepared spells.
You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of druid spells requires time spent in prayer and meditation: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.
Spellcasting Ability
Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your druid spells, since your magic draws upon your devotion and attunement to nature. You use your Wisdom whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Wisdom modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a druid spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier
Ritual Casting
You can cast a druid spell as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag and you have the spell prepared.

Spellcasting Focus
You can use a druidic focus as a spellcasting focus for your druid spells.

cards.name: Shapeshifting
cards.effect: Assume an unlocked prepared form or revert early. Apply engine HP, equipment, concentration and reserve rules. This is not a spell and cannot copy monster stat blocks.

source.originalText:
Shapeshifting
At 1st level, you gain the ability to transform into various animal forms. Shapeshifting is Aethel's native druidic transformation discipline and functions according to the following rules:

Activation and Duration
You can use a bonus action to assume a beast form. You can remain in beast form for 10 minutes per use. You then revert to your normal form unless you expend another use of this feature. You can revert to your normal form earlier by using a bonus action on your turn.

Uses per Day
At 1st level, you can use your Shapeshifting ability twice per long rest. You gain additional uses as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Shapeshifting Uses column of the Druid table.

Available Forms
At 1st level, you can transform into any of the Base Druid Forms listed below. At 11th level, you gain access to Arch Druid Forms. At 10th level, you gain access to Hero Druid Forms specific to your chosen Circle.
Limitations While Transformed
While in beast form:
You cannot cast spells unless specified by your Hero Class
Your ability to speak is limited (only preserved in arch/hero forms)
You retain your mental ability scores (Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma)
You gain the physical traits of the chosen form as specified

Starting at 18th level, the primal magic that you wield causes you to age more slowly. For every 10 years that pass, your body ages only 1 year.

source.originalText:

At 20th level, you can use your Shapeshifting feature an unlimited number of times.

cards.name: Bonus Cantrip
cards.effect: Learn one additional Druid cantrip. Choose one terrain package for Circle Spells at 3/5/7/9; preserve exact source spell pairs and ordinary rank gates.

source.originalText:
Bonus Cantrip
When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you learn one additional druid cantrip of your choice.

cards.name: Natural Recovery
cards.effect: Restore ceil(Druid level/2)RP, capped by maximum. This is a finite added recovery, not spell slots or multiplied by rank. RP remains fungible; preserved source rank 6 spending restriction is not used in this simplified draft.

source.originalText:
Natural Recovery
Starting at 2nd level, you can regain some of your magical energy by sitting in meditation and communing with nature. During a short rest, you choose expended Resonance Points to recover. The Resonance Points can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your druid level (rounded up), and none of the points can be used to cast spells of 6th level or higher. You can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.
For example, when you are a 4th-level druid, you can recover up to 2 Resonance Points during a short rest.
Circle Spells
Your mystical connection to the land infuses you with the ability to cast certain spells. At 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level you gain access to circle spells connected to the land where you became a druid. Choose that land, arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp, or Murk, and consult the associated list of spells.
Once you gain access to a circle spell, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.

cards.name: Land's Stride
cards.effect: Ignore nonmagical difficult terrain and ordinary plant thorns. Advantage on saves against magically created/manipulated plants impeding movement. Does not bypass walls, fire or nonplant restraint.

source.originalText:
Land's Stride
Starting at 6th level, moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard.
In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement, such as those created by the entangle spell.

cards.name: Nature's Ward
cards.effect: Immune to Charmed/Frightened from fey/elementals, poison damage, Poisoned and disease. Does not suppress all creature abilities or remove an existing curse.

source.originalText:
Nature's Ward
When you reach 10th level, you can't be charmed or frightened by elementals or fey, and you are immune to poison and disease.

cards.name: Blight Elk

Blight Elk

Antlers: Your antler attack deals 2d8 piercing damage
Toxic Presence: Plants wither in your presence, and water becomes tainted

source.originalText:
Tanglemaw

cards.name: Nature's Sanctuary
cards.effect: Before roll target WIS save; failure chooses another legal target or attack misses. Success immune to this feature 24 hours. Creature knows requirement; area effects and indirect hazards unaffected.

source.originalText:
Nature's Sanctuary
When you reach 14th level, creatures of the natural world sense your connection to nature and become hesitant to attack you. When a beast or plant creature attacks you, that creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your druid spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature must choose a different target, or the attack automatically misses. On a successful save, the creature is immune to this effect for 24 hours.
The creature is aware of this effect before it makes its attack against you.

cards.name: Combat Shapeshifting
cards.effect: Restore 1d8 real HP per RP paid, never beyond maximum. Does not restore temporary buffer or shift uses. No Dissonance as class technique; cannot heal after form ended/incapacitated.

source.originalText:
Combat Shapeshifting

cards.name: Circle Forms

source.originalText:
Circle Forms

cards.name: Primal Strike

source.originalText:
Primal Strike

source.originalText:
Elemental Shapeshifting

source.originalText:
Storm Magic
